notes: THE LOAD-BEARING CASE FOR INSTANT ARITHMETIC. Two slots straddle a US Eastern DST transition. In both, the local wall-clock difference between start and end is wrong, in opposite directions: fall-back reads 30 minutes for a 90-minute service, spring-forward reads 2 hours for a 60-minute service. Any implementation that computes duration, overlap, or reminder offsets by subtracting local clock labels produces a double-booked or short-changed appointment. Subtracting the RFC 3339 instants gives the right answer in both cases with no DST-specific code.

cases.why_it_breaks: 01:00 to 01:30 looks like 30 minutes. The hour 01:00-02:00 local occurs twice on this date, so the label 01:30 is ambiguous and only the offset disambiguates it.
01:30 to 03:30 looks like 2 hours. The hour 02:00-03:00 local does not exist on this date, so no slot may start inside it.

then.overlap_rule: Two slots overlap if and only if their UTC instant ranges intersect. Wall-clock comparison is never sufficient.
then.reminder_offsets: A reminder N minutes before the appointment is start_utc minus N minutes, not a local-clock subtraction.
then.equal_instants_compare_equal: 2026-11-01T05:00:00Z and 2026-11-01T01:00:00-04:00 are the same slot boundary and MUST compare equal.

wrong_answers.behaviour: compute duration by subtracting local clock labels
wrong_answers.why: Yields 30 minutes for a 90-minute massage and 2 hours for a 60-minute consult. The first double-books the practitioner for the hour it thinks is free; the second blocks an hour that is actually available.

wrong_answers.behaviour: emit timestamps without an offset and rely on the business timezone
wrong_answers.why: 2026-11-01T01:30:00 in America/New_York is ambiguous: it names two distinct instants an hour apart.

wrong_answers.behaviour: emit a slot starting at 2026-03-08T02:30:00 local
wrong_answers.why: That local time does not exist. Clocks jump from 02:00 EST to 03:00 EDT.

wrong_answers.behaviour: normalize every timestamp to a fixed offset for the whole day
wrong_answers.why: The offset changes within the day, so one of the two boundaries will be wrong by an hour.
